title: Current Program - SharkSmart
text:
Current Program - SharkSmart

NSW Shark Management Program

The NSW Shark Management Program is the largest and most comprehensive program of its kind in the world, with the NSW Government investing approximately $120 million over the next two years to help keep people safer in the water.

No government can promise there will never be another shark incident. What we can do is keep investing in technology, research and education that help reduce risk and better protect people using our beaches.

From 1 July 2026, 72 ocean beaches (including all 38 Sydney beaches) benefit from dawn to dusk drone monitoring 365 days of the year, including at least one beach in every coastal local government area.

Expanded regional operations along the coast include flights every weekend throughout the year, daily flights from 1 December to 30 April, and extended daily flight hours to cover dawn to dusk. This is additional to the existing school holiday drone program along the coast.

The other components of the NSW Shark Management Program include 305 SMART drumlines across 19 LGAs all year; 51 shark nets across eight LGAs between Newcastle and Wollongong from 1 September 2026 to 31 March 2027; 37 tagged shark listening stations at ocean beaches; and 2 tagged shark listening stations in Sydney Harbour.

When a tagged target shark swims within 500m of a tagged shark listening station, an alert is sent to the public via the SharkSmart App and X. SMART drumlines are currently deployed daily, weather dependent, from Tweed Heads to Pambula.
